localContext: Mount Prospect's housing stock, largely 1950s and 1960s brick ranches and split-levels, often includes original single-skin steel garage doors. Many of these doors lack insulation. problemSigns.sign: Loud grinding or squealing as the door moves
problemSigns.detail: This sound indicates metal-on-metal friction or failing bearings within the rollers. It's often the first sign of wear.

problemSigns.sign: Door shudders or vibrates in the track
problemSigns.detail: Uneven movement suggests rollers are no longer rolling smoothly. They may be dragging or binding.

problemSigns.sign: Visible flat spots or wobble on rollers
problemSigns.detail: Inspect the rollers when the door is open. Flat spots or an off-center wobble mean the roller surface is compromised.
Rust weakens the roller stem, leading to breakage. A bent stem prevents the roller from tracking correctly.
